notes.front: What is the initial aeronautical knowledge test for the remote pilot certificate, in one sentence?
notes.back: The FAA's multiple-choice exam "Unmanned Aircraft General – Small" (UAG), taken at an FAA-approved knowledge testing centre.
notes.explanation: Passing it is the usual route to the certificate, and it is the exam this deck prepares you for.
notes.example: A first-time drone pilot books the UAG at a testing centre and brings government-issued photo ID.
notes.source: FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot" (updated 9 June 2026); FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · FAA "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot" page, updated 9 June 2026

notes.front: What is a flight review, for a pilot of manned aircraft?
notes.back: A periodic check of at least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training, given by an authorised instructor.
notes.explanation: A manned-aircraft pilot needs a recent one (within the last 24 calendar months) to act as pilot in command; part 107 lets such pilots take a shorter route to the remote pilot certificate.
notes.example: A private pilot flies an hour with an instructor and spends an hour reviewing the operating rules; the instructor signs the pilot’s logbook to record it, and the flight review is done.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.56 Flight review, paragraphs (a) and (c) (eCFR); 14 CFR § 107.65
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: For part 107, who counts as a "part 61 pilot", in one sentence?
notes.back: Someone holding a part 61 pilot certificate, other than a student pilot certificate, who meets the flight review requirements of § 61.56.
notes.explanation: Part 107 gives such pilots a different route: online training instead of the knowledge test.
notes.example: A private aeroplane pilot with a flight review completed within the previous 24 months.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (d)(2); FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot"
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: How is a period in calendar months counted?
notes.back: In whole months: the period ends on the last day of its final month, not on the same date.
notes.explanation: Many part 107 deadlines use calendar months, so they always fall at the end of a month.
notes.example: A test passed on 13 September 2020 plus 24 calendar months runs to 30 September 2022 (AC 107-2A, Figure 6-1).
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.7.2, Figure 6-1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: What is part 107 recurrent training, in one sentence?
notes.back: Online FAA training, at no cost, that a certificated remote pilot completes to keep their aeronautical knowledge current.
notes.explanation: It replaced the recurrent knowledge test, which the FAA stopped offering on 6 April 2021.
notes.example: A wedding videographer completes the FAA Safety Team's "Part 107 Small UAS Recurrent" course (ALC-677) online.
notes.source: FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot" (updated 9 June 2026); FAA, "Changes to Testing for a Remote Pilot Certificate" (5 April 2021)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · FAA "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot" page, updated 9 June 2026

notes.front: What is aeronautical knowledge recency, in one sentence?
notes.back: The rule that you may use remote PIC privileges only if you passed the test or completed qualifying training within the previous 24 calendar months.
notes.explanation: It is recency, not a new certificate, that keeps you flying legally: fall outside the window and you must not act as remote PIC until you catch up.
notes.example: A pilot who passed the test on 13 September 2020 had to complete recurrent training by 30 September 2022.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.65 Aeronautical knowledge recency (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.7.2
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What is IACRA, in one sentence?
notes.back: The FAA's online Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application system, used to apply for the remote pilot certificate.
notes.explanation: It is the fastest route: knowledge test results upload to it, though the FAA says a result may take up to 48 hours from the test date to appear in IACRA.
notes.example: After passing the UAG, an applicant logs into IACRA, starts an application and enters the 17-digit Knowledge Test Exam ID.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.4.1; FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot"
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: What is an FTN, in one sentence?
notes.back: An FAA Tracking Number, created in IACRA, which every applicant needs before registering for an airman knowledge test.
notes.explanation: Required since 13 January 2020, it is printed on your test report in place of the old applicant ID number.
notes.example: Step 1 on the FAA's "Become a Drone Pilot" page: create an IACRA profile to get your FTN, then book the UAG.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.6
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: What is a temporary remote pilot certificate, in one sentence?
notes.back: A remote pilot certificate issued for up to 120 calendar days, until the permanent certificate is issued.
notes.explanation: It lets a qualified applicant fly while the permanent certificate is processed and mailed.
notes.example: After the security check, an applicant gets an email and prints a temporary certificate from IACRA.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.64 Temporary certificate (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.4.1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What is the airman knowledge test report (AKTR), in one sentence?
notes.back: The printed report of your knowledge test score, handed to you as soon as you finish the test.
notes.explanation: It also lists the codes of the topics you answered wrongly, which shows what to revise; keep the original.
notes.example: You leave the testing centre with your AKTR showing a pass, and use it to apply in IACRA.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Introduction and Appendix 3

notes.front: What is a U.S. agent for service, in one sentence?
notes.back: An entity or adult (18 or over) with a U.S. address whom a certificate holder or applicant names to receive FAA service for them.
notes.explanation: Individuals with a foreign address and no U.S. physical address on file with the FAA must designate one to hold or use a remote pilot certificate.
notes.example: A pilot whose only address is in Canada names a U.S. relative, aged 18 or over, as agent.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 3 as of that date

notes.front: Who may act as remote PIC?
notes.back: Normally, only someone holding a remote pilot certificate who also meets the aeronautical knowledge recency requirement.
notes.explanation: Holding the certificate is not enough on its own; recency must be current too. § 107.12(c) allows an exception for a foreign-registered aircraft flown with FAA authorisation.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.12 Requirement for a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (eCFR), (b)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: When may a person without a remote pilot certificate fly a small UAS under part 107?
notes.back: Normally, only under the direct supervision of a remote PIC who can immediately take direct control of the flight.
notes.explanation: This lets trainees and clients fly, with the remote PIC able to deal with any hazard at once.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.12 Requirement for a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (eCFR), (a)(2); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.2.2
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Your friend, who has no certificate, flies your drone while you stand across the field, too far away to reach the controls, with no way to override. Is this allowed?
notes.back: No: as remote PIC you must be able to immediately take direct control.
notes.explanation: AC 107-2A lists ways to keep that ability: a second, overriding control station, standing close enough to take over, or an automated "safe" mode you can trigger.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.12 Requirement for a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (eCFR), (a)(2); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.2.2
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Your recency has lapsed. May you still fly a small UAS under part 107?
notes.back: Only as a person manipulating the controls, directly supervised by a current remote PIC who can take over immediately.
notes.explanation: AC 107-2A says a remote pilot who has not met recurrent training may fly this way, but may not act as remote PIC.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.2.2; 14 CFR § 107.12
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: May the FAA let an airman fly a foreign-registered civil small UAS without an FAA remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: Yes: the FAA may authorise it, consistent with international standards.
notes.explanation: This is an exception to the general certificate requirement in § 107.12.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.12 Requirement for a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (eCFR), (c)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: To be eligible for a remote pilot certificate, you must be at least {{c1::16}} years old.
notes.explanation: You can take the knowledge test from age 14, but the certificate itself needs 16.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (a)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What English-language ability must an applicant for a remote pilot certificate have?
notes.back: The ability to read, speak, write and understand English.
notes.explanation: If a medical reason prevents one of these, the FAA may instead place operating limitations on the certificate.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (b)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What medical condition makes an applicant ineligible for a remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: Knowing, or having reason to know, of a physical or mental condition that would interfere with safe operation of a small UAS.
notes.explanation: No medical certificate is required; the test is what the applicant knows or should know.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (c)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: How must an applicant demonstrate aeronautical knowledge for a remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: By passing the initial knowledge test or, for a part 61 pilot, completing training on the § 107.74 knowledge areas.
notes.explanation: The part 61 training (course ALC-451 on the FAA Safety Team site) covers 8 of the test's 13 knowledge areas, leaving out topics such as airspace and radio procedures.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (d); FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot"
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What is the minimum age to take the remote pilot knowledge test?
notes.back: 14 years old.
notes.explanation: The ACS sets 14 for the test, while § 107.61 sets 16 for the certificate.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 1, "Knowledge Test Requirements"

notes.front: A 15-year-old passes the knowledge test. Can she be issued a remote pilot certificate now?
notes.back: Not yet: she must be 16. Her passing test report stays valid for 24 calendar months.
notes.explanation: She may test at 14 but must wait until 16 for the certificate.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR); FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendices 1 and 3
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: A private pilot whose flight review was 10 months ago wants a remote pilot certificate. Must she pass the knowledge test?
notes.back: No. As a part 61 pilot she may complete the online part 107 training instead (or take the test if she prefers).
notes.explanation: Part 61 pilots meeting § 61.56 may choose either route.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (d)(2); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.4.1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: A student pilot holding only a part 61 student pilot certificate asks to use the online-training route. Can he?
notes.back: No. Student pilot certificates are excluded, so he must pass the knowledge test.
notes.explanation: The part 61 route needs a pilot certificate other than a student pilot certificate, plus a current flight review.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.61 Eligibility (eCFR), (d)(2)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: On which FAA form do you apply for a remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: FAA Form 8710-13, normally completed online in IACRA.
notes.explanation: A paper application is possible, but AC 107-2A recommends IACRA so non-part-61 applicants can get a temporary certificate.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.4.1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: What security check must an applicant pass before a temporary remote pilot certificate is issued?
notes.back: Vetting by the Transportation Security Administration; failing it means no temporary or permanent certificate.
notes.explanation: An applicant who believes they wrongly failed the security threat assessment may appeal to the TSA.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.5
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: On the part 61 route, can a certificated flight instructor issue you a temporary certificate?
notes.back: No. A flight instructor can process the application, but cannot issue a temporary certificate.
notes.explanation: An FAA Flight Standards office, an FAA-designated pilot examiner, or an airman certification representative (at a pilot school) can issue one.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.4.2, Note; FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot"
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: A temporary remote pilot certificate is issued for up to {{c1::120 calendar days}}.
notes.explanation: A permanent certificate is then issued to an applicant the FAA finds qualified.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.64 Temporary certificate (eCFR), (a)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Besides its printed expiry date, when else does a temporary remote pilot certificate expire?
notes.back: When you receive the permanent certificate, or a notice that the certificate is denied or revoked.
notes.explanation: Whichever of the three events comes first ends it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.64 Temporary certificate (eCFR), (b)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Your temporary certificate shows an expiry date next month, but your permanent certificate arrived today. Which one is valid from today?
notes.back: Only the permanent certificate: the temporary one expires on receipt of the permanent.
notes.explanation: The printed date is just one of three ways a temporary certificate ends.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.64 Temporary certificate (eCFR), (b)(2)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: To act as remote PIC, you must have passed the test or completed qualifying training within the previous {{c1::24 calendar months}}.
notes.explanation: This is aeronautical knowledge recency; the FAA's online recurrent training is the usual way to renew it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.65 Aeronautical knowledge recency (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Which three things each satisfy aeronautical knowledge recency?
notes.back: Passing the initial knowledge test, completing recurrent training, or (part 61 pilots) completing the § 107.74 training.
notes.explanation: Each must have been done within the previous 24 calendar months.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.65 Aeronautical knowledge recency (eCFR), (a)–(c)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Is there still a recurrent knowledge test for remote pilots?
notes.back: No. The recurrent test (UGR) ended on 6 April 2021; recurrent training replaced it.
notes.explanation: Older study material may still mention the recurrent test.
notes.source: FAA, "Changes to Testing for a Remote Pilot Certificate with a Small Aircraft Rating" (5 April 2021)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · FAA "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot" page, updated 9 June 2026

notes.front: You passed the knowledge test on 13 September 2020. By what date must you complete recurrent training to keep acting as remote PIC?
notes.back: 30 September 2022.
notes.explanation: 24 calendar months run to the end of the month, not to the 13th.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.7.2, Figure 6-1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: Your recurrent training is due by 30 September 2020, but you complete it early, on 15 July 2020. When is the next one due?
notes.back: By 31 July 2022.
notes.explanation: The new 24 calendar months count from the month you actually trained, so training early brings the next deadline forward.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.7.2, Figure 6-1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: Your recency ran out at the end of September, and you complete recurrent training on 5 October. May you act as remote PIC on 2 October?
notes.back: No. You may not exercise the certificate's privileges from 1 October until the training is done.
notes.explanation: AC 107-2A, Figure 6-1, shows exactly this gap; the next training is then due 24 calendar months after October.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶6.7.2, Figure 6-1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: After failing the knowledge test, you may not reapply for it for {{c1::14 calendar days}}.
notes.explanation: No instructor endorsement is needed to retest.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.71 Retesting after failure (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: You failed the knowledge test on 1 March. What do you need in order to retest?
notes.back: Wait 14 calendar days and bring the failed test report; no instructor endorsement is needed.
notes.explanation: The testing centre needs the report showing the failure before you retest.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 1; 14 CFR § 107.71

notes.front: What score passes the remote pilot knowledge test?
notes.back: 70% or better.
notes.explanation: § 107.67(c) leaves the pass mark to the FAA; the ACS sets it at 70%.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 1

notes.front: For applying for the remote pilot certificate, how long is a passing knowledge test report valid?
notes.back: 24 calendar months.
notes.explanation: Apply within that window, or you will need to pass the test again.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 3

notes.front: What happens to someone the FAA finds has cheated on a knowledge test?
notes.back: A 1-year ban on applying for any certificate, rating or authorization or taking any test; certificates held may be suspended or revoked.
notes.explanation: Cheating includes copying the test, getting help, using unauthorised aids, or testing for someone else.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.69 Knowledge tests: Cheating or other unauthorized conduct (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What can a Federal or State drug conviction (for example, for selling or possessing drugs) lead to?
notes.back: Denial of an application for up to 1 year after the final conviction, or suspension or revocation of a remote pilot certificate.
notes.explanation: The same applies to acts barred by § 91.17(a) (alcohol and drug limits for crewmembers) or § 91.19(a) (knowingly carrying illegal drugs).
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.57 Offenses involving alcohol or drugs (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: An applicant was convicted under State law of selling marijuana, with the final conviction 8 months ago. Can the FAA deny the application?
notes.back: Yes: it may deny it for up to 1 year after the date of final conviction.
notes.explanation: After a certificate is issued, the same conviction could instead ground suspension or revocation.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.57 Offenses involving alcohol or drugs (eCFR), (a)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What can refusing a law enforcement officer's alcohol test (under § 91.17(c)) lead to?
notes.back: Denial of an application for up to 1 year after the refusal, or suspension or revocation of a remote pilot certificate.
notes.explanation: Refusing to furnish, or authorise release of, test results the FAA requests has the same consequences.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.59 Refusal to submit to an alcohol test or to furnish test results (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: After a flight, a remote pilot refuses a police officer's lawful request for a breath alcohol test. What can the FAA do?
notes.back: Suspend or revoke the remote pilot certificate.
notes.explanation: For someone still applying, the FAA could deny the application for up to 1 year after the refusal.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.59 Refusal to submit to an alcohol test or to furnish test results (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: After changing your permanent mailing address, you may not use your certificate beyond {{c1::30 days}} unless you have told the FAA.
notes.explanation: Notify the FAA Airman Certification Branch by letter or through the FAA website.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.77 Change of name or address (eCFR), (c)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: You moved house 6 weeks ago and have not told the FAA. May you act as remote PIC today?
notes.back: No. More than 30 days have passed, so you must notify the FAA of the new address first.
notes.explanation: The 30 days run from the date of the address change.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.77 Change of name or address (eCFR), (c)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What must accompany an application to change the name on a remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: The certificate itself and a document proving the change, such as a marriage licence or court order.
notes.explanation: The documents are returned after inspection.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.77 Change of name or address (eCFR), (a)–(b)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: If you voluntarily surrender your remote pilot certificate, how could you get one again?
notes.back: Only by meeting the eligibility and application requirements again (§§ 107.61 and 107.63).
notes.explanation: The signed surrender statement says the certificate will not be reissued otherwise.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.79 Voluntary surrender of certificate (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: An individual with no U.S. physical address has not designated a U.S. agent for service. What follows?
notes.back: They may not exercise part 107 certificate privileges, and cannot be issued a certificate.
notes.explanation: Changes to the agent or the agent's details must be notified to the FAA within 30 days.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 3 as of that date

notes.front: What is the difference between the minimum age for the knowledge test and for the remote pilot certificate?
notes.back: Test: 14. Certificate: 16.
notes.explanation: A young applicant can pass early; the passing report stays valid for 24 calendar months.
notes.source: FAA-S-ACS-10B, Appendix 1; 14 CFR § 107.61(a)

notes.front: What is the difference between the knowledge test and recurrent training?
notes.back: The knowledge test is the initial exam at a testing centre; recurrent training is the free online course that keeps you current afterwards.
notes.explanation: Either one, taken within the previous 24 calendar months, satisfies recency.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.65 Aeronautical knowledge recency (eCFR); FAA, "Become a Certificated Remote Pilot"
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date
